title: Closed-form left powers in para-Cayley–Dickson algebras
statement: Let A_0 = ℝ and A_m = A_(m−1) × A_(m−1) with (a, b)(c, d) = (ac − conj(d) b, d a + b conj(c)) and conj(a, b) = (conj(a), −b) (the real Cayley–Dickson algebras, dimension 2^m). Define the para-product x ∗ y = conj(x) conj(y) and the left powers p_1 = x, p_(k+1) = p_k ∗ x. For every m ≥ 0, every x ∈ A_m and every j ≥ 0: p_(2j+1) = n^j x and p_(2j+2) = n^j conj(x)^2, where n = n(x) is the sum of the squares of the coordinates of x; equivalently (x ∗ x) ∗ x = n(x) x. Remarks with proofs: left-to-right binary powering B(1) = x, B(2a) = B(a) ∗ B(a), B(2a+1) = B(2a) ∗ x returns p_e for every e = 2^j − 1 (j ≥ 1) and every e = 2^j − 2 (j ≥ 2), and B(4) = p_4 if and only if x^4 = n(x) conj(x)^2 (x = 1 + e_1 gives B(4) = −4, p_4 = −4 e_1); the identity (x ∗ y) ∗ x = n(x) y holds for every y ∈ span{1, x} but fails for general y in every A_m with m ≥ 4 (x = e_1 + e_10, y = 1 + e_4). Additions of the note: the binary-powering remarks and the explicit witness.

bases: Elduque, Composition algebras, arXiv:1810.09979: Theorem 3.2 with Examples 3.4 (dimension ≤ 8: the identity whose case y = x is the Theorem)
Biss–Dugger–Isaksen 2008, Comm. Algebra 36(2), doi:10.1080/00927870701724094: Definition 2.1, Section 2, Lemma 3.6 (the identities of Lemma 1, every dimension)
